title: regime_overhaul: /frameworksInScope
description: rbi-it-outsourcing-md-2023 is still in frameworksInScope, but for NBFCs RBI repealed it on 28 Nov 2025. It was replaced by the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/363). Chapter IV and the IT-specific provisions of Chapter II apply to NBFCs in the Middle Layer and above, and this entity's RBI registration N-13.09999 is nbfc-middle-layer. The successor has no vocab id and no instruments.json entry lists rbi-it-outsourcing-md-2023 in supersedes[], so instrument_superseded cannot be expressed. The profile is left unchanged and the regime change is flagged for re-review. Timing caveat: the repeal predates the catalog retrievedAt (2026-09-14), and the catalog version string already records it. It is reported because the profile was never refreshed and the repeal falls inside the 24-month window. Third-party IT and cyber arrangements outside the outsourcing directions fall under rbi-cyber-tech-directions-2026 paras 126-135, which is already in scope. From: rbi-it-outsourcing-md-2023 (in scope as a binding instrument). To: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025, RBI/DOR/2025-26/363 (no vocab id). Effective date: 2025-11-28.

description: src/tools/args.ts's zEJSON() (lines 78-90, used for find/export filters and every non-vector-search aggregation stage) is `z.object({}).loose()` with no maxItems on the enclosing pipeline array and no maxLength/pattern on keys or values; DBOperationArgs.database and CollOperationArgs.collection (mongodbTool.ts:11-17) are plain z.string() with no length cap or character allow-list, unlike CommonArgs.string()'s NO_UNICODE_REGEX in the same repo (args.ts:22-23). This is an input-validation gap on the tool-call surface, not a rate-limiting mechanism, which this codebase does not implement at all for MCP tool calls.

title: MongoDB MCP tool schemas carry no personal-data classification markers
description: src/tools/mongodb/mongodbSchemas.ts:1-107 (and, by extension, every mongodb/* tool argsShape it feeds) defines filter, projection, document and pipeline fields as opaque EJSON or `.passthrough()` records with only a `.describe()` prose hint (e.g. `zAutoEmbedVectorSearchStageParams`, `VectorSearchStage`). No field, in this file or anywhere under src/tools/mongodb, carries a data-classification annotation (x-data-classification, x-dpdp-category, @pii or equivalent), although applications/mcp-gateway/README.md and applications/mcp-gateway/env/{qa,prod}.json declare the connected client-data and order stores pii + financial. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0. zEJSON is defined as z.object({}).loose() in src/tools/args.ts:88-90; .passthrough() appears only in find.ts:22 and create/createIndex.ts:164, not in mongodbSchemas.ts itself.

title: find tool returns full unmasked documents from pii/financial collections
description: src/tools/mongodb/read/find.ts:108-118: FindTool.execute EJSON-serialises the entire cursor result set (`EJSON.stringify(cursorResults.documents)`) and returns it verbatim to the MCP client; the only applied limits are `config.maxBytesPerQuery` and `config.maxDocumentsPerQuery`, neither of which masks or filters fields. env/qa.json and env/prod.json both declare dataClassification [pii, financial] for this app. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: aggregate tool returns full unmasked pipeline results
description: src/tools/mongodb/read/aggregate.ts:187-192: AggregateTool.execute EJSON-serialises and returns the entire aggregation result set for an arbitrary user-supplied pipeline; pipelines containing `$out`/`$merge` (lines 134-141) write to a collection and send back no documents, so they are not an additional data-return path, but the read branch's result set still carries no masking or classification filter before being returned to the client. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: export tool writes full unmasked documents to an unencrypted local file
description: src/tools/mongodb/read/export.ts:68-98: ExportTool.execute streams the full find/aggregate cursor to a local JSON file via ExportsManager.createJSONExport with no field mask and no encryption-at-rest on the export file; the file is exposed to the caller via a resource URI and, on stdio transport (isServerRunningLocally(), lines 131-133), its plain filesystem path. Cleanup relies on ExportsManager.close() deleting the session export directory and a best-effort TTL sweep (config.exportTimeoutMs, default 300000ms), not immediate purge. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: CreateDBUserTool returns a newly generated password in plain text
description: src/tools/atlas/create/createDBUser.ts:84-96: when the tool auto-generates a password, the success content text is `User "${username}" created successfully with password: \`${password}\`.`, sent as the raw JSON-RPC tool result. `this.session.keychain.register(password, "password")` runs immediately before, but keychain-based redaction (loggerBase.ts) only scrubs subsequent logger output, not the direct tool-result payload that reaches the MCP client transcript. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: MCP HTTP transport has no default authentication requirement
description: src/transports/mcpHttpServer.ts:306-319: setupMiddlewares() is the only request gate on the HTTP transport; it loops over `Object.entries(this.userConfig.httpHeaders)` and rejects a request only if a configured header value mismatches. `httpHeaders` defaults to `{}` (src/common/config/userConfig.ts:136-143), so with no operator configuration the loop performs zero comparisons and `next()` is always called: every JSON-RPC tool call is reachable unauthenticated over HTTP once the transport binds beyond loopback (httpHost defaults to 127.0.0.1; the repo's AWS Dockerfile sets host 0.0.0.0 and the Azure bicep binds to '::'). Consistent with this, deploy/azure/bicep/params_template.json ships `authMode: NOAUTH` by default; a proper Azure-AD OIDC auth config exists only as an opt-in second template. env/prod.json lists this app's prod environment as exposure: partner with dataClassification [pii, financial]. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: Core MongoDB tool arguments accept unbounded, unvalidated input that reaches the driver
description: src/tools/args.ts:78-90: `zEJSON()` (`z.object({}).loose().transform(toEJSON)`) accepts any key/value pair with no maxItems on enclosing arrays (AggregateArgs.pipeline, defined at src/tools/mongodb/read/aggregate.ts:47-49) and no maxLength/pattern on keys or values, and is used as the schema for find/export `filter` and for every aggregation stage that is not `$vectorSearch`. src/tools/mongodb/mongodbTool.ts:11-17 defines `DBOperationArgs.database` and `CollOperationArgs.collection` as plain `z.string()` with no length cap or character allow-list, unlike `CommonArgs.string()` (args.ts:22-23), which applies `NO_UNICODE_REGEX` and is used for the Atlas tool arguments in the same repo. mcpHttpServer.ts:307 enforces express.json({limit: httpBodyLimit}) (default 100 KiB) and result-side caps (maxDocumentsPerQuery, maxBytesPerQuery) exist, but neither validates individual field length/shape, so per-field input validation is still missing. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.
